inputs.name: dating formula
inputs.cite: claim file B4d formal statement (Z22903977 s5)

day.reading: dates come from k = mu and are then cited as confirmation of it; the mutation rate was re-fitted to keep the date; no independent measurement enters (pgenetics@L16; B4d q1-q2)
day.holds: every date from T = D/(2 mu) assumes k = mu per generation, whatever calibrates mu (B4d analysis); the twofold lower pedigree mu doubles the date, the direction Day describes (Keightley 2012); McCarthy (B4e) and Hossjer (B4f) state the same dependence

critic.reading: clock dates also rest on calibrations that do not come from k = mu; 'sole practical application' is absolute
critic.holds: a pedigree mu is measured without a date, and Langergraber 2012 dates the split at >= 7-8 My without fossil calibration, so the date is not derived from itself; Day's own Z18525185 applies k = mu to predict 630 fixations (C6 q2, M-302), a use other than calibration

notes: Inference; the two positions answer different questions. Day's holds for 'is the date independent of the k = mu assumption' (no: every clock date uses it). The critics' holds for 'is the date derived from the identity and then cited for it' (not for a pedigree-mu date: mu is measured, not fitted). Whether agreement between fossil-calibrated and pedigree dates tests k = mu is B4d's open external question. The 'sole' wording meets a counter-example in Day's own corpus (C6). No verdict.
